status: Planned before observing benchmark test outputs; launch only after first benchmark finishes
question: Does increasing full-image input resolution from 224 to 320 pixels change development-selected discrimination, calibration and frozen-threshold behavior?

arms.additional: 320 pixels, same architectures, seeds, cohort hashes, augmentation fractions, optimizer, batch size and selection rules

rationale: More spatial detail may affect image classification; this is a matched sensitivity analysis, not a claim of improved clinical performance.
budget: Launch sequentially. Additional audit/training cap is min(180 minutes, 300 minutes minus observed first-run runtime minus 20 minutes export reserve). Skip if insufficient budget for all nine trials. Early stopping retained.
selection: Each resolution retains its own development-selected architecture. If one combined export is desired, compare architecture-resolution mean selection AUROC only; ties prefer 224 then alphabetical architecture. No test-dependent choice.
reporting: Report all 18 trials and both resolution-selected ensembles; primary architecture benchmark remains intact. Mark resolution comparison as a protocol extension and exploratory.
limitations: Expanded selection search increases selection optimism
Equal time limits do not guarantee equal convergence
External testing remains necessary for transportability claims
